correctness.rationale: The identity follows from PQP=aP and QPQ=aQ: C²=−a(P−Q)², and (P−Q)²C=(1−a)C. If a is neither 0 nor 1, C cannot vanish (commutation would force a=a²) and the cubic prevents nilpotence. For an independent census, fix the image U and kernel W of P and choose the image line of Q first. If it equals U, the q^m choices contribute P and q^m−1 square-zero commutators. Each image line in W contributes q^(m−1) commuting choices and (q−1)q^(m−1) nonzero square-zero choices. The other image lines have unique representatives u+w with w≠0 and u a fixed generator of U. For each such line, a prescribed trace a imposes ψ(u)=a and ψ(w)=1−a on the projecting functional, giving q^(m−1) choices. Trace 0 gives square zero; at trace 1 the unique functional vanishing on W gives square zero and the other q^(m−1)−1 give index three; other traces give nonnilpotence. This recovers all four counts including q=2 and m=1. The index-three construction just requires two nonzero orthogonal vectors in W and so works over every field for m≥2. Inspected the finite-field verifier and its scope as frozen evidence; no frozen code was run.
